text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.
LONDON - Shares closed firm as Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's latest warning against an over-valued Wall Street proved a damp squib and gilts were pulled higher by strong German bunds.
The FTSE 100 index closed 9.9 points higher at 4,339.2, with gainers in a two-to-one majority.

FRANKFURT - Shares shrugged off worries on Wall Street over the course of bourse trade and rose to new highs. The DAX index, which measures floor trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended up 38.85 points at a record 3,276.72 points.
The IBIS DAX index for electronic trade lost momentum in afternoon dealings to trade shy of record highs. In late trade the IBIS DAX index stood at 3,272.58 points.
PARIS - Shares closed markedly higher despite a fall on Wall Street, pushed by fresh liquidity and corporate as well as economic forecasts.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 27.23 points or 1.05 percent at 2,629.40.
ZURICH - After initial advances to an all-time high, Swiss shares ended a volatile day back down near the day's lows. Dealers said the session was marked by selective buying and special situations.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index fell 6.87 points to 2,869.81.
TOKYO - Stocks staged a comeback by the end of the session, recovering from the morning's losses which came in reaction to warnings by Greenspan over dramatic advances on Wall Street.
The 225-share Nikkei average edged back above the 19,000 level to finish 30.64 points, or 0.16 percent, higher at 19,021.56.
HONG KONG - Stocks shrugged off Greenspan's comments to end higher, buoyed by interest in China-related issues and selective buying amid the blue chips.
The Hang Seng Index rose 4.77 points, or 0.04 percent, to close at 13,546.60.
SYDNEY - Shares finished weaker, weighed down by a Wall Street fall after Greenspan made cautionary comments in his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
The All Ordinaries index closed 18.4 points lower at 2,464.7, just off its intra-day low of 2,464.4.

JOHANNESBURG - Gold shares, helped by a weaker rand and a firmer bullion price, sparkled towards the close of a mixed trading session. Industrials limped for most of the day after an overnight dive on Wall Street, a weaker rand and nervousness over hawkish comments by Greenspan.
The gold index ended the day 44.6 points higher at 1,588.1, while the industrial index sagged 55.1 points to 8,323.7, leaving the overall share index 10.0 points lower at 7,195.7.
